title: pm daily scratchpad - launch prep + PRD edits
content:
Quick morning scratchpad - focus on Hosted API launch checklist and PRD edits. Lots of follow-ups today, keeping notes here so I don't lose anything.

Top priorities:
- Finalize PRD section on rollout policy (canary + auto-fallback) — need engineering sign-off by EOD.
- Confirm infra readiness for burst capacity tests scheduled Thu. Ops asked for load curve by Wed.
- Lock down messaging for release notes and docs (DX to review).

PRD edits (items to add/resolve)
- Scope: clarify Dedicated vs Hosted behavior for model pinning. Currently ambiguous; add example sequence showing pinned model + fallback to quantized variant.
- Rollouts: specify criteria for automatic promotion from canary (error rate < 0.5%, latency p95 < target, no regressions on sample prompts). Add measurement windows (15m, 1h).
- Failure modes: add flow for capacity shortage -> auto-fallback to cheaper model variant + notif to customer. Who owns notif copy? CS/Comms.
- Acceptance criteria: add checklist for SRE runbook and runbook links (INF-SRE-runbook-v2).

Stakeholder follow-ups (who to ping)
- @Luca (serving-runtime): need sign-off on kernel-selection text and example config.
- @Priya (console): confirm rollout UI copy and canary toggle behavior.
- @Ben (SRE): ask for burst test schedule + runbook authors.
- @Elena (legal): quick confirm on data retention language for Hosted tenants.

Meeting notes (sync 10:30 with eng + ops)
- Luca: kernel selection looks good, wants clearer limits on sequence-length assumptions. Action: add note and example sequence-length table.
- Ben: SRE will run a small-scale burst test Wed then scale to full Thu. Need test dataset and traffic shaping plan. Action: create test traffic plan and share by Tue.
- Priya: Console team can ship canary toggle but needs API flag names and feature flag timeline. Action: propose flag names by EOD.

Launch checklist (working, not exhaustive)
- [ ] PRD final version committed + linked in Confluence
- [ ] Engineering sign-off on rollout criteria (Luca)
- [ ] SRE runbook created and reviewed (Ben)
- [ ] Burst capacity test run and results documented
- [ ] Release notes draft for doc site + changelog (DX)
- [ ] Customer comms ready for enterprise customers with dedicated capacity
- [ ] Telemetry dashboards created (latency/cost per-token, error rates, model fallback rate)
- [ ] Post-launch rollback plan documented

Open questions / risks
- What is our fallback model latency delta? Need measurement to set sensible thresholds. (Luca to provide numbers)
- Pricing impact of auto-fallback for customers: finance input needed. Add to FIN ticket.
- Edge case: token-level caching interactions when switching model mid-session. Potential mismatch; engineering to comment.

Notes to self (quick)
- Draft release note intro: "Redwood Hosted API: improved rollout controls, model fallbacks, and cost-aware routing — now with canary deploys and automatic fallbacks to keep apps online." Keep shorter.
- Remember to attach sample prompts used for evals to the PRD (folder: /evaluations/hosted-api/rollout-samples).
- Slack thread: #prod-launch — post final checklist and call for onsite coverage Fri.

Time-blocking for today
- 9:00-10:00: update PRD sections + add example tables
- 10:30-11:00: sync with eng + ops (notes above)
- 11:30-12:00: ping stakeholders and gather sign-offs
- 13:00-14:00: draft release notes + docs outline for DX
- 15:00-16:00: finalize canary UI flag naming with Priya

Small TODOs (one-liners)
- Add runbook link to PRD
- Create JIRA ticket for finance on pricing impact (INF-4389 linked above)
- Upload sample prompts to evals folder
- Confirm meeting invite for Thu burst test

Rough text to paste into PRD (draft)
"Rollout policy: The platform supports staged rollouts via canary deployments. A canary cohort (default 1-5% traffic) is evaluated over configurable windows. Promotion criteria: error rate stable below 0.5% over 15m window and latency p95 below target for two consecutive windows. On promotion failure, automatic rollback will occur and an incident notification will be sent to the account owner. In cases of capacity shortage, the router may route to an approved fallback model variant; customers will be notified and metrics will log fallback rate."

End of scratchpad for now — will iterate after EOD sign-offs.

Unresolved: still need finance + legal check. Mark as follow-ups for tomorrow if not resolved today.

-- Aisha
